scope: Book/chapter browsing, paged exact search, finite reading sessions and offline navigation. No source text, audio or artwork changes.

additionalChecks: Pinned Arabic and English candidate inventories reproduce unchanged
Packaged public files and offline hashes

realBrowser: Both existing English and Arabic blocks rendered exactly as the canonical source: eight blocks compared.
Book page opens both available hadith, with accessible source actions and an honest notice that chapter headings are unavailable.
Starting a session at Hadith 2, browsing back to Hadith 1 and returning home preserves Continue to Hadith 2, including after reload.
The packaged reader saved successfully, then reopened after its local HTTP server was stopped. Book browsing and exact search for intentions succeeded.
With that server still stopped, Cedar played across the natural 37.512-second boundary into Hadith 2 and the reading view followed. Playback remained active with no media error at 47 seconds.
Day/night appearance and the largest reading size were exercised. No horizontal overflow at 320px; the compact dock also fits a synthetic entry with no available recording.

syntheticLibrary.publication: Local temporary directory only; source candidates and synthetic fixtures are excluded from Pages.
checks: Book selector and source-ordered chapter routes, including a 51-entry chapter split into 30 and 21 results.
All 95 matching synthetic records reachable across search pages of 30, 30, 30 and 5; returning from the last result restores page 4 and its query.
A five-minute plan beginning at 100 contains [100,103,106,109,112], correctly crossing a book boundary and nonconsecutive labels.
Browsing onward to 115 leaves the session continuation at 112. Finish preserves separate unread marks; Next session begins at 115.
Unknown bookmarks are retained, invalid routes are explicit, and empty or mismatched chapter maps are rejected by automated checks.

limitations: Desktop browser checks do not establish iPhone locked-screen behavior for this release.
